issues.legal_issue: Whether a court must conduct a preliminary inquiry and hear a proposed accused before making a complaint that may lead to prosecution for an offence connected with a document produced in court proceedings.
material_facts: The respondent was accused of submitting forged documents in proceedings before revenue authorities acting as courts.
A revenue appellate authority directed that an FIR be registered, without first conducting an inquiry or hearing the respondent.
The High Court quashed the FIR on the ground that an inquiry and opportunity to be heard were required.
Supreme Court decisions expressed conflicting views on whether an inquiry and hearing were required before a complaint was made.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not resolve whether a preliminary inquiry or an opportunity to be heard was mandatory. It directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice for appropriate orders to refer the questions to a larger Bench.
issues.legal_principle: Section 195(1)(b)(ii) restricts cognizance of specified offences concerning documents produced or given in evidence in court proceedings, and Section 195(3) includes qualifying revenue courts within the meaning of court. Section 340 permits a court, after such preliminary inquiry, if any, as it thinks necessary, to make a complaint. Pritish v. State of Maharashtra held that a preliminary inquiry and pre-complaint hearing are not mandatory; Amarsang Nathaji v. Hardik Harshadbhai Patel relied on Pritish, while Sharad Pawar v. Jagmohan Dalmiya required an inquiry and hearing without explaining its departure from Pritish. The Court also noted the relevant observations in Iqbal Singh Marwah v. Meenakshi Marwah and referred the conflict for larger-Bench consideration.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_quashing: The matter came before the Supreme Court in a criminal appeal challenging the quashing of criminal proceedings.
predicates.conflicting_authoritative_views: Earlier Supreme Court decisions stated conflicting requirements for inquiry and hearing before a court makes a complaint leading to prosecution.
predicates.unresolved_procedural_requirement: The appeal raised whether a preliminary inquiry and an opportunity for the proposed accused to be heard were required before the complaint.
predicates.question_referred_to_larger_bench: The Court directed that the question be placed for consideration by a larger Bench.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal from quashing presents an unresolved procedural requirement and authoritative decisions conflict on it, the question is referred for larger-Bench consideration.
